title: Ending a Free Study session should show a Summary
description:
A Free Study session can never reach the Summary screen, so closing one drops the user straight back to Home with no wrap-up at all.

Root cause: SessionViewModel.close() (Sources/Features/Session/SessionViewModel.swift ~line 295) opens with 'guard !isFreeStudy else { return }', so it returns before doing anything, and phase never becomes .finished. Free Study also never auto-finishes by design — advanceFreeStudy() pulls endlessly from FreeStudySource — so .finished is unreachable for that path. HomeView's session cover only renders SummaryView when 'activeSession.phase == .finished', hence: no summary, straight Home.

Where it came from: T091 (Summary buttons reworked to Free Study on top, Back home below). That task's spec states the Summary's Free Study button must work 'after BOTH a normal SRS session AND a Free Study session (the owner confirmed a Free Study session's summary should also offer Free Study again)'. The first half works and was verified; the second half is unreachable today because no Free Study summary exists. T091's wiring already handles it correctly if such a summary ever appears — HomeView's onStartFreeStudy reads activeSessionDeck and the finished session's mode, both of which are set for a free-study session — so this is purely about producing the summary, not about re-wiring the button.

What would need deciding (NOT decided here): whether a Free Study session should end on a summary at all; if so, what it shows. Free Study deliberately records no CardSchedule and no DailyStats, so the grade-count grid (Again/Hard/Good/Easy) would be all zeros and the streak line may not be meaningful — cardsWritten and elapsed time are tracked in memory and would be real. SummaryView already takes an isFreeStudy flag (currently passed but only lightly used), which suggests a free-study variant of the screen was anticipated. Implementation would likely mean letting the free-study path through close() into finish(), or giving it its own finish.

Why it matters: it's the one gap knowingly left open when T090/T091 were completed and merged by hand on 2026-07-25, and it makes an explicitly-stated owner requirement silently non-functional.

title: Brush angle lock: PencilKit findings for a later attempt
description:
The user wants to lock the brush nib to a chosen angle so the pen can be held at whatever grip is comfortable without changing how the stroke inks. Built twice and removed twice on 2026-07-25 (commits 07c931f, ef34015, 1a3e32a, reverted in fc1b2b2) because the angle never reached the ink. Capturing the measurements so a later attempt does not repeat them.

What was tried:
1. Squeeze-and-roll: read the roll off UIPencilInteraction.Squeeze.hoverPose and set it as the ink angle. Never engaged at all — hoverPose is nil unless the pencil is hovering in range, so a squeeze made away from the screen reported no roll and the gesture fell through to clear/release.
2. A brush menu with an angle dial (deterministic, no dependence on pose). The dial worked — verified on the iPad sim: sets the angle, panel switches to "Angle locked", unlock works — but the ink still did not change.
3. Rewriting the finished stroke so every PKStrokePoint carries the locked azimuth.

What was MEASURED (all on the iPad sim, Xcode 26 SDK):
- PKInk carries only inkType + color. There is no azimuth on the ink; the angle lives on PKInkingTool and on each PKStrokePoint.
- .fountainPen IS azimuth-sensitive. Rendering the same synthetic stroke at azimuth 0 vs pi/2 via PKDrawing.image(from:scale:): at point size 3 -> 624 vs 1248 ink pixels; 6.5 -> 1312 vs 5680; 12 -> 3436 vs 12796; 24 -> 8370 vs 28990; 40 -> 15010 vs 51994. .pen and .monoline showed ZERO difference (round nibs), .marker and .crayon were sensitive. So the visual effect the user wants is real and large, even at simulator stroke widths.
- PKInkingTool(inkType:color:width:azimuth:) (iOS 26+, typechecks fine) changed a simulator-drawn stroke by exactly 0 pixels.
- The stroke rewrite provably works in isolation: azimuth 0 -> 1.5708, ink pixels 8372 -> 28990 on a PKCanvasView drawing set directly.
- On the live canvas it never took. Logging confirmed the rewrite RAN on device with the correct angle (angle=1.5708, firstAz=-3.14, size=6.57pt, points=16) yet the rendered stroke was byte-identical. Assigning drawing from inside canvasViewDrawingDidChange appears to be discarded when PencilKit finishes its own update; hopping to the next main-actor turn changed 0 pixels -> 60 pixels (edge noise, not a rotation — a real rotation quadruples ink coverage).
- canvasViewDidEndUsingTool is NOT a usable hook: it fires before the stroke is in drawing at all (logged strokes=0).

Open question for whoever picks this up: whether the live PKCanvasView can be made to honour a per-point or tool azimuth at all, or whether this needs the ink to be drawn outside PencilKit. Worth checking on real Pencil Pro hardware first — every measurement above is from simulator touches, and it is possible PKInkingTool azimuth only takes effect when a real pencil supplies an azimuth to override. Anchors: Sources/Features/Session/Canvas/WritingCanvas.swift, and the removed BrushMenu.swift/PencilSqueeze.swift in commit 1a3e32a.

Why it matters: the user asked for this twice and explicitly said they want to come back to it later.

title: Deck offers Start writing but the session has no cards to serve
description:
A deck can offer "Start writing" on the deck setup sheet while the session that then starts has nothing to serve, leaving the user on a session screen where "Show answer" does nothing and no grade buttons ever appear.

Observed on 2026-07-25 as a UI smoke-test failure (Tests/UITests/SmokeFlowTests.swift:57 — "The grade row should appear after revealing the answer"), on a simulator whose app data had accumulated from a lot of manual grading that day. The test asserts startedSession BEFORE that line and that assertion passed, so a session genuinely started; it was the reveal that produced nothing. Uninstalling the app and re-running passed immediately, confirming it is data-state dependent rather than a code regression.

Likely mechanism: the deck card / setup sheet decides whether to offer a normal SRS session from DailyAllowance, while SessionViewModel builds its queue separately and filters out cards already completed today (Sources/Features/Session/SessionViewModel.swift, buildEntries skips ids in completedTodayIDs). When those two disagree, the sheet offers "Start writing" but queue.next() returns nil at init, so phase becomes .caughtUp. In .caughtUp, ActionRowView still renders the Show answer button (srsLayout only swaps in the grade row when phase == .revealed), and showAnswer() guards on phase == .prompt — so the button is present and inert. Anchors: SessionViewModel.init (the else branch setting .caughtUp), ActionRowView.srsLayout, and wherever the setup sheet chooses between "Start writing" and Free Study.

What is NOT decided here: whether the fix belongs in the availability calculation (so the sheet stops offering a session that has no cards), in the session (so an empty queue routes somewhere sensible instead of a dead screen), or both — and what the user should see instead.

Why it matters: it is a dead end in the primary flow, it is invisible until it happens, and it can also make the local Definition-of-Done gate fail spuriously as the day progresses.
